final_answer:
Yes, AI-10-49 treatment leads to significant global changes in chromatin accessibility,
but the nature of the change is a REORGANIZATION rather than a simple global gain or loss.

KEY FINDINGS:

1. PEAK COUNT REDUCTION (-22.8%): AI-10-49-treated cells have significantly fewer
   ATAC-seq peaks (mean 50,924 vs 65,998 in DMSO). There are 39,179 DMSO-only peaks
   (38.0% of the consensus set) versus only 13,263 AI-10-49-only peaks (12.9%),
   indicating a net loss of accessible chromatin regions.

2. TOTAL SIGNAL IS MAINTAINED: Despite losing ~23% of peaks, total ATAC-seq signal
   is nearly identical between conditions (ratio = 0.997). The same total amount of
   open chromatin is redistributed across different genomic locations.

3. RETAINED PEAKS BECOME STRONGER AND WIDER: Peaks present in AI-10-49 have 26.3%
   higher mean signal intensity (8.21 vs 6.50) and are 14.6% wider (median 118 vs
   103 bp). Signal density increases by 14.7% (0.0565 vs 0.0493 signal/bp).

4. STATISTICAL SIGNIFICANCE: Four independent genome-wide tests confirm the global
   shift is highly significant (Wilcoxon p ~ 0, KS p = 2.8e-161, Mann-Whitney p =
   1.6e-164), though the per-peak effect size is modest (rank-biserial r = -0.099).

5. NO GENOMIC COMPARTMENT BIAS: The proportion of peaks in promoters (10.7%), exons
   (5.6%), introns (54.0%), and intergenic regions (30.9%) is similar across shared,
   DMSO-only, and AI-10-49-only peaks.

BIOLOGICAL INTERPRETATION:
CBFβ-SMMHC inhibition causes loss of many weak, diffuse accessible regions (likely
aberrant CBFβ-SMMHC-dependent binding sites) and consolidation at fewer, stronger,
wider accessible regions (likely canonical RUNX1 targets). This is consistent with
the known mechanism where CBFβ-SMMHC forms an aberrant complex with RUNX1 that
redistributes DNA binding genome-wide.

CAVEATS: With only 2 biological replicates per condition, individual peak-level
statistical testing has very limited power (no peaks pass FDR < 0.05). The global
tests are robust, but specific differentially accessible loci should be validated
with additional replication.
